sections.title: Sets up shared test match
sections.what: Creates one even match model where both players win 65 percent of points in a best-of-three match, and one fresh starting score with no points played and player A serving.
sections.why: Likely reason: most checks use the same even match and clean start, so one shared setup keeps the tests consistent.
sections.watch_out: Many expected values depend on these shared values, so changing them changes many results at once.

sections.name: tennis: iid point model
sections.title: Checks tennis win-probability rules
sections.what: Checks that a 65 percent point win chance gives about an 83 percent game hold. Checks deuce and advantage handling, tiebreak serve order and odds, and that equal players are shown as even. Also checks that the stronger player is favoured, that the Pressure Index is a percentage, and that impossible scores raise an error.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The checks cover the rules a tennis fan would expect the model to follow.
sections.watch_out: Some checks compare rounded values, so a small change in the formula can pass one check and fail another.

summary: Tests the tennis win-probability model: how likely a player is to win a game, tiebreak, set and match from a given score, and how much each point matters.
purpose: Makes sure the tennis maths gives the expected answers, rejects impossible scores, and matches known tennis rules such as tiebreak serve order and deuce.
why: Likely reason: the model is used to show pressure and win chances, so wrong numbers would mislead fans. Reason not stated in the code for the exact choice of tests.
how: Sets up one even match (both players win 65 percent of points, best of three) and one clean starting score. Then runs groups of checks: game hold chance, game points and deuce, tiebreak serving and odds, match odds, point importance and the Pressure Index. Each check compares the model output to an expected value or throws an error for invalid input.
inputs: Test data only: a model with win chance per point for each player and the number of sets, and score states with sets, games, points and the server.
outputs: Pass or fail results from the test runner. No files or database are changed.
risks: Expected values are rounded, so a small change to the model may still pass some checks and fail others. Invalid-input checks rely on specific error types.
debug: If a test fails, look at the named check and compare its expected value with the model output. Check the model file that holds the win chance formulas. Start with the hold probability and the match win checks, since many others build on them.
